section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contains the opening header for the Purim 5711 maamar.
section.t: B'Siyata D'Shmaya.
Purim 5711*

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the acceptance of Purim was specifically during the low point of Haman's decree, surpassing even the high point of the Giving of the Torah, due to their mesirus nefesh.
section.t: "And the Jews accepted that which they had begun to do,"
and the Rebbe, my father-in-law, explains in his maamar beginning with the words "Zeh"
(which has just been published)
that they accepted what they had begun at the time of the Giving of the Torah.
For their saying "We will do and we will hear" was only a beginning
("they had begun to do"),
and in the days of Achashverosh
(at the time of Haman's decree)
was the acceptance,
"and the Jews accepted."
And he notes precisely regarding this,
that at first glance it is an astonishing thing,
for at the Giving of the Torah, Israel was at the ultimate level of elevation,
both physically, as they were then in the most excellent state and condition regarding the matter of freedom,
and spiritually, as there was then for them a revelation of G-dliness at the most sublime level,
and in the days of Achashverosh, Israel was at the ultimate level of descent,
for in addition to the concealment and hiding that is in every exile, "and darkness will cover the earth,"
with numerous tzimtzumim, concealments, and hidings,
then,
(at the time of Haman's decree)
the concealment and hiding was even greater,
and also physically they were then at the lowest state, utterly,
for the decree was to destroy, kill, and annihilate, G-d forbid, all the Jews, from youth to elder, infants and women, in one day,
and nevertheless,
at the time of the Giving of the Torah,
when Israel was at the ultimate level of elevation,
there was only the beginning
("they had begun to do"),
and at the time of Haman's decree,
when they were at the ultimate level of lowliness,
specifically then they accepted what they had begun at the Giving of the Torah.
And he explains regarding this,
that at the time of the decree,
their fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos was with mesirus nefesh.
[And it is worth noting,
that in the maamar "Vekibel HaYehudim"
it is explained,
that their mesirus nefesh at that time was that if they had converted from their religion, G-d forbid, nothing would have been done to them,
for the decree was only against the Jews,
and nevertheless, no extraneous thought entered their minds, G-d forbid.
And he explains,
that their mesirus nefesh was
(not only not to deny [their faith], G-d forbid,
but they also gave their lives)
for the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos,
to the extent that they gathered congregations in public to study Torah with mesirus nefesh.]
And the arousal of their mesirus nefesh was through Mordechai the Jew,
the Moshe of that generation,
who gathered congregations in public to strengthen their faith.
And the main
work of Mordechai was in the study of Torah with young schoolchildren,
who are the foundation of all of Israel
[as is explained at length in the maamar
regarding the greatness of the merit of the breath of young schoolchildren],
as it is stated in the Midrash
that Mordechai the Jew gathered twenty-two thousand students
and taught them Torah with mesirus nefesh,
to the point that when Haman the wicked came and Mordechai said to them, "Flee, lest you be burned by my coal," they said, "We are with you, whether for life or for death,"
for they accepted upon themselves any punishment that might come, solely in order not to be separated from the Torah.
And this is "And the Jews accepted that which they had begun to do,"
that at the Giving of the Torah there was only the beginning, and at the time of Haman's decree was the acceptance,
for through their having actual mesirus nefesh for Torah and mitzvos at that time, they were elevated
(in one aspect)
to a more sublime level than they were at the time of the Giving of the Torah,
and therefore
specifically then was the acceptance,
"and the Jews accepted."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions why the maamar details Mordechai's work with schoolchildren and the physical aspects of the Jews' state, when the core point is about mesirus nefesh.
section.t: B)
And it must be understood,
the point of the explanation in the maamar is that specifically at the time of the decree was the acceptance, due to their mesirus nefesh,
so what relevance is there here that the arousal of their mesirus nefesh was through Mordechai, and that the main work of Mordechai was the study of Torah with young schoolchildren?
And also, an explanation is needed regarding what is stated with precision
(at the beginning of the maamar)
that at the time of the Giving of the Torah, Israel was at the ultimate level of elevation, and at the time of the decree they were at the ultimate level of lowliness,
and this was both spiritually and physically.
For at first glance,
according to the precision of the maamar,

how is it possible that at a time when they were at the ultimate level of elevation there was only the beginning, and at a time when they were at the ultimate level of lowliness, specifically then was the acceptance?
The elevation and lowliness in their spiritual state is relevant,
so why does the maamar bring that the elevation at the time of the Giving of the Torah and the lowliness at the time of the decree were also physical?
